title: Markets: Sunday 25 October

morning.session_note: Sunday edition · what's new since Saturday, and the week ahead. Markets were shut on Saturday; dashboard prices are Friday's closes.
summary: US officials gave mixed signals on Iran. On Friday envoy Tom Barrack said a US strike "this weekend" was "absolutely" possible, Trump told a Florida rally the US "may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree", and, asked about Barrack's remark, said "If that's the case, I don't know anything about it"; the White House had said on Thursday there would be no strikes before the 3 November midterms ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-oil-gas-prices-strait-of-hormuz-midterms/), [Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/world/trump-says-us-may-do-another-little-epic-fury-targeting-iran-6108171), [Ynet](https://www.ynetnews.com/article/hj0xogyhfg)). On Saturday the Houthis said they targeted Saudi oil sites including Yanbu and the East-West pipeline; Saudi authorities have not confirmed any hits. Brent settled at US$116.72 on Friday, before these developments.

Moody's left France at Aa3 with a negative outlook after a periodic review late on Friday, when bond markets had been pricing in a downgrade, saying the rating assumes a deficit-reducing 2027 budget is adopted ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/moodys-holds-steady-on-frances-credit-rating-as-country-grapples-with-turmoil-and-higher-yields.html), [franceinfo/AFP](https://www.franceinfo.fr/economie/l-agence-moody-s-maintient-la-note-souveraine-de-la-france-a-aa3-avec-perspective-negative_8251510.html)). Monday is the first bond trading session since the decision; France's 10-year yield hit 5.14% on Thursday, its highest since July 2002 ([Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/unresthit-france-poised-for-moodys-ratings-verdict-4968793)).

This week brings Australian CPI (11:30am Wednesday), the Fed (5am Thursday Sydney time), the ECB and BoJ, and results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon. CBA expects September-quarter trimmed mean inflation of 1.0%, above the RBA's 0.8% forecast, with ASX rate futures implying a 56% chance of a 3 November hike at Friday's close ([CommBank](https://www.commbank.com.au/articles/newsroom/2026/10/inflation-cpi-rba-interest-rates-november.html), [RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)).

cards.headline: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report in the same week as the Fed
cards.takeaway: Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report in the same week as the Fed, GDP and PCE, after an October selloff in chip and AI shares.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday covered last week's selloff. The week-ahead previews from Reuters and Saxo, and the reporting schedule, are new.
cards.key_figure: About 890 US companies report this week, including 34 worth more than US$100 billion (Saxo)
cards.what_happened: Microsoft, Alphabet, ServiceNow and Ford report on Wednesday US time, and Amazon, Eli Lilly, Intel and SanDisk on Thursday, with Exxon Mobil and Chevron on Friday ([Saxo](https://www.home.saxo/en-gb/content/articles/equities/week-ahead-26-30-oct-23102026)). About a third of S&P 500 companies report this week, and Reuters said investors will gauge whether the results can extend the AI rally after growing wary of the risks of data-centre spending ([Reuters Take Five via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/take-five-ai-trade-meets-the-fed-4968194)). The SOXX semiconductor ETF is down about 16% in October and the Nasdaq-100 about 5%, according to Saxo.
cards.why_it_matters: The results come after a week in which investors moved into Treasuries on worries about the debt tech companies are taking on to build AI networks ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/bonds-yields-us-treasurys.html)). Saxo said Wall Street is demanding "proof of monetisation" from AI spending.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard (Friday close): S&P 500 7,623.7 (−0.5% week); Nasdaq 25,955.3 (−0.7% week); VIX 19.45.
cards.what_to_watch: Microsoft and Alphabet results land on Thursday morning Sydney time, a few hours after the Fed; Amazon on Friday morning.

cards.headline: RBC and Morningstar stayed positive on Zip after its 29.5% fall
cards.takeaway: RBC kept an outperform rating and Morningstar called the shares materially undervalued; RBC also flagged higher loss rates, and US bad debts rose.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday reported the fall and the A$10.1 million fraud cost. The analyst views and the bad-debt and leadership details are new.
cards.key_figure: Zip US net bad debts: 1.93% of transaction volume, up from 1.51% (AAP)
cards.what_happened: Zip said it had "identified and contained" a coordinated US fraud, in which people opened new accounts with legitimate credentials to make unpaid transactions. US net bad debts rose to 1.93% of transaction volume from 1.51%, and its US president Joe Heck resigned, as announced on 16 October ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/buy-now-pay-later-company-s-shares-plunge-on-us-fraud)). Zip kept its FY27 guidance of more than 30% US transaction-volume growth and, Capital Brief reported, group cash EBITDA of A$340 million ([Capital Brief](https://www.capitalbrief.com/briefing/zip-reaffirms-fy27-guidance-after-posting-17-growth-in-q1-income-956f9ced-5461-4d66-b74d-e5f060ed37ff/)).
cards.why_it_matters: RBC's Julian Mulcahy noted the stock also sold off steeply when loss rates jumped in the second quarter of FY26. Chief executive Cynthia Scott said customers were using Zip more often and the company was well positioned for the holiday season. AAP reported the shares are down 63.6% this year.

competing_views.view: Kept an outperform rating and A$2.07 target, saying the quarter beat on most metrics but loss rates were higher and the fraud would hit profit.
Said the shares are "materially undervalued" and described the fraud, credit and funding headwinds as temporary, with guidance holding.

cards.what_to_watch: Monday's trading; the AGM on Thursday 19 November, which will vote on a proposed five-for-one share consolidation.

cards.headline: Wednesday's CPI is the test for a 3 November RBA hike
cards.takeaway: The big four banks expect trimmed mean inflation of 0.9–1.0% for the quarter, above the RBA's 0.8% forecast; rate futures and prediction markets put different odds on a hike.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday covered the futures pricing, the big four's calls and tonight's Sarah Hunter interview. CBA's headline, fuel and services forecasts, the prediction-market odds and the Wednesday timing of Governor Bullock's Senate appearance are new.
cards.key_figure: CBA forecast: trimmed mean +1.0% q/q, 3.6% y/y; headline +1.3% q/q, 3.9% y/y
cards.what_happened: CBA's Trent Saunders expects trimmed mean inflation of 1.0% in the September quarter, compared with the RBA's August forecast of 0.8%, and headline CPI of 1.3%. CBA forecasts fuel prices rose 9.8% in September and annual market services inflation rose to 4.3% from 4.1%. It still expects a hold but called the meeting "live" ([CommBank](https://www.commbank.com.au/articles/newsroom/2026/10/inflation-cpi-rba-interest-rates-november.html)). ASX 30-day interbank futures put the chance of a hike at 56% at Friday's close, while prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi put it at 68% ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)).
cards.why_it_matters: A hike would take the cash rate from 4.60% to 4.85%, the fifth increase this year. CBA said the decision will depend on both the headline result and what drives it, including whether price pressures look more broad-based or persistent, particularly in services. Governor Bullock and other RBA executives appear before a Senate committee at 11:15am Wednesday, 15 minutes before the CPI release ([RBA Coming Up](https://www.rba.gov.au/coming-up/)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: AU 2Y 4.92% (±0 bp week) and AU 10Y 5.28% (−4 bp week), both as at 21 Oct, the latest RBA data; curve +36 bp; AUD/USD 0.7006 (+0.8% week).
cards.priced_in: Futures imply an expected cash rate of 4.74% after the meeting, about halfway to a full 25 bp hike (RBA Watch, 23 Oct close).

comparison.title: Chance of a 3 November RBA hike
comparison.why_different: The futures figure is derived from the expected cash rate priced into ASX 30-day interbank futures; the prediction-market figure reflects bets placed on Polymarket and Kalshi, weighted by money traded, and is not derived from interest-rate pricing.

rows.measure: Implied probability of a 25 bp hike
rows.method: Implied post-meeting rate of 4.74% against 4.60% now

competing_views.view: Baseline is a hold, but the decision will depend heavily on the outcome and composition of the CPI.
Expect a 25 bp hike in November.

cards.what_to_watch: Sarah Hunter on 60 Minutes at 8:40pm tonight (pre-recorded on 21 October); Bullock at the Senate committee at 11:15am and CPI at 11:30am Wednesday.

cards.headline: The Fed is expected to hold this week and keep a December hike open
cards.takeaway: Treasury yields fell over the week, and markets put only a small chance on a move on Wednesday but most on a December hike.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday reported CNBC's FedWatch figure. Saxo's odds for this week's meeting and its preview are new.
cards.key_figure: Fed funds range: 3.75–4.00%; hike odds about 10% this week, about 75% for December (Saxo, Friday)
cards.what_happened: The Fed meets on Tuesday and Wednesday US time after raising rates in September. Saxo said market odds of a hike this week were about 10% by Friday and about 75% for December, and that falling yields and the AI selloff had weakened the case for back-to-back moves ([Saxo](https://www.home.saxo/en-gb/content/articles/equities/week-ahead-26-30-oct-23102026)). CNBC, citing CME FedWatch, put the December chance at about 71% ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/bonds-yields-us-treasurys.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: There are no new Fed projections at this meeting, so PIMCO said Chair Kevin Warsh's framing of the hold and the number of dissents matter more than the decision itself. The decision lands hours before Microsoft and Alphabet report, and US GDP and September PCE inflation follow the next day ([BEA](https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: US 10Y 5.00% (−9 bp week); US 2Y 4.69% (−5 bp week); gold futures 4,007.9 (−4.1% week).

competing_views.view: Does not expect Chair Warsh to "green light a December meeting rate hike".
Expects a hold with "a clear tightening bias", and a 25 bp hike in December as the most likely next move.

cards.what_to_watch: Decision and statement at 5am Thursday Sydney time; GDP and PCE at 11:30pm Thursday.

sections.note: Weekend developments after Friday's close are not yet reflected in any market price.

cards.headline: US officials gave mixed signals on new strikes on Iran
cards.takeaway: A US envoy said a strike this weekend was possible and Trump mentioned "another little Epic Fury", after the White House ruled out strikes before the midterms; Iran said it offered to reopen Hormuz if the US lifts its blockade.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday covered Trump's "end it quickly or let it wind down" remarks. Barrack's comments, Trump's rally remarks, Iran's Saturday statements and Friday's Istanbul meeting are new.
cards.what_happened: Asked by podcast host Mario Nawfal on Friday whether a strike could come this weekend, US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack said "Absolutely", adding that Trump is "open and available and accessible to a deal"; Barrack has no direct role on Iran policy ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-oil-gas-prices-strait-of-hormuz-midterms/), [Epoch Times](https://www.theepochtimes.com/world/trump-says-us-may-do-another-little-epic-fury-targeting-iran-6108171)). The White House said on Thursday the US would not resume attacks before the 3 November midterms ([Ynet](https://www.ynetnews.com/article/hj0xogyhfg)). At a Florida rally on Friday Trump said "We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree", and asked about Barrack's remark he said "If that's the case, I don't know anything about it" (Epoch Times). On Saturday Iran's armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi said "We will not allow U.S. military ships in the Persian Gulf under any circumstances", and Iran's ambassador to Pakistan said Tehran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the US lifted its naval blockade, a proposal he said Trump rejected (CBS News). On Friday in Istanbul, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt called in a joint statement for unrestricted passage through the strait ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/24/iran-says-wont-allow-us-warships-to-get-close-as-trump-ponders-new-attacks)).
cards.why_it_matters: French foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot, speaking in Istanbul after meeting counterparts including from the UK, Germany and Saudi Arabia, said further escalation between Iran and the US "would leave no winners and would likely have very serious consequences" for hydrocarbon prices (CBS News, AFP). None of the weekend developments is reflected in Friday's closing prices.

competing_views.view: "If they're smart, they'll just say, 'Let's get down to business.' But, you know, I doubt they'll do that because perhaps they're not smart."
"A new attack on Iran would widen the war and spread the conflict across the region."

cards.what_to_watch: Any strike or US statement before oil futures reopen on Monday morning Sydney time; Israel's election on Tuesday.

cards.headline: Houthis say they targeted Saudi oil sites, including the Hormuz bypass pipeline
cards.takeaway: The group named Yanbu, the Rabigh refinery and the East-West pipeline; the coalition said it shot down two missiles, and it was not clear if any hit.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday covered attacks on Dammam and Shaybah. The Houthis' Saturday statement naming the Rabigh refinery, the East-West pipeline and Riyadh airport, and the coalition's interceptions, are new; the group had also said it targeted Yanbu earlier in the week (CNBC).
cards.key_figure: Brent futures: US$116.72 at Friday's settle, the highest settlement since 29 April (snapshot, CNBC)
cards.what_happened: The Houthis said they targeted King Khalid airport in Riyadh, Aramco's Yanbu facilities, the Rabigh refinery, crude pumping stations on the East-West pipeline and King Fahd airport in Dammam. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two missiles heading for Yanbu and Taif, and Saudi civil defence reported falling debris in the Mecca and Medina regions. Saudi authorities did not comment directly on the Houthi statements, and it was not clear if any hit ([Reuters via ThePrint](https://theprint.in/world/houthis-say-they-attacked-saudi-oil-sites-strikes-reported-in-aden/3080805/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/24/saudi-led-coalition-says-it-intercepted-houthi-ballistic-missiles-.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: The East-West pipeline carries Saudi crude to Yanbu on the Red Sea, letting Riyadh send much of its exports around the Strait of Hormuz; Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser has said its volume rose from 2 million to 7 million barrels a day (CBS News). Friday's 3.1% rise in Brent followed the earlier Houthi attacks and an oil spill off the UAE (Reuters via The Star).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard (Friday close, before the weekend attacks): Brent futures 116.72 (+3.1% day, +6.2% week); FRED Brent spot 115.22 as at 20 Oct, lagged.
cards.what_to_watch: Any Aramco or Saudi statement on damage; Brent's open on Monday morning Sydney time.

cards.headline: Marisks says October is the most intense month for Hormuz attacks since March
cards.takeaway: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two supertankers hit mines, after claiming seven ship incidents on Thursday; none had been corroborated, and Trump said Iran was "making up fake hits".
cards.new_since_last_issue: The Revolutionary Guards' supertanker statement, the route dispute and the Marisks and UKMTO tallies are new since Saturday.
cards.what_happened: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said seven tankers were attacked or hit mines overnight into Thursday, and on Friday that two supertankers struck mines ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/24/iran-says-wont-allow-us-warships-to-get-close-as-trump-ponders-new-attacks), [CGTN](https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-10-24/Iran-reports-tanker-blasts-in-Hormuz-as-Trump-hints-at-renewed-strikes-1RuSG1ODy0M/p.html)). None of Thursday's claimed incidents had been corroborated, according to CBS News and AFP, and Trump wrote on Truth Social that Iran was "making up fake hits, mines, and everything else" ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-trump-us-oil-gas-prices-strait-of-hormuz-midterms/)). Greece-based consultancy Marisks told Reuters October is "the most intense period of maritime attacks" around the strait since March, and UKMTO, the UK maritime security agency, had logged 135 incidents linked to the conflict as of 16 October (CGTN).
cards.why_it_matters: The claims sit on a dispute over routes: Iran demands that ships seek its authorisation and use a northern route near its coast, while the US has encouraged a southern route near Oman and escorted tankers along it. Iran said all the ships it reported on Thursday had used the US-backed lanes (CBS News).
cards.what_to_watch: Confirmation of the vessels and any UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) advisories.

cards.headline: Moody's left France at Aa3 when bond markets had priced in a cut
cards.takeaway: The rating stays one notch above S&P and Fitch, with a negative outlook tied to political fragmentation and the 2027 budget.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday's issue went out before the decision. The outcome and reactions are new.
cards.what_happened: In a periodic review that it said was not a rating action, Moody's said the rating "assumes that a deficit-reducing budget for 2027 will be adopted, while financing costs and social tensions will abate somewhat", and that the negative outlook reflects the risk that political fragmentation "will continue to impair the functioning" of parliament ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/23/moodys-holds-steady-on-frances-credit-rating-as-country-grapples-with-turmoil-and-higher-yields.html), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/unresthit-france-poised-for-moodys-ratings-verdict-4968793)). Prime Minister Lecornu said the decision shows lenders "there is a path", and the finance ministry credited the budget's credibility ([franceinfo/AFP](https://www.franceinfo.fr/economie/l-agence-moody-s-maintient-la-note-souveraine-de-la-france-a-aa3-avec-perspective-negative_8251510.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: France's 10-year yield hit 5.14% on Thursday, its highest since July 2002, and its spread over German bonds was the widest in 15 years (Reuters). The government is struggling to pass the 2027 budget, which targets a deficit of 5% of output, and the finance ministry has forecast debt of 121.7% of GDP in 2027 (CNBC).

competing_views.view: "You want to wait and see how the narrative evolves over the next six months into the election. That's going to have a more meaningful impact on the spread."

competing_views.who: Mike Bell, RBC BlueBay Asset Management
competing_views.view: Said pressure could grow after the presidential vote if Moody's, S&P and Fitch all cut France to BBB, potentially forcing sales by investors with rating limits.

cards.what_to_watch: French yields and the spread over Germany on Monday; whether Lagarde addresses French spreads at the ECB on Thursday.

cards.headline: Elections in Brazil and Israel bracket the week
cards.takeaway: Brazil's presidential runoff is on Sunday local time, and Israel votes on Tuesday.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Israel's election was in Saturday's calendar. Brazil's runoff, Reuters' read on the Israeli polls and the West Bank lockdown are new.
cards.what_happened: Brazil holds a runoff on Sunday between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro ([Saxo](https://www.home.saxo/en-gb/content/articles/equities/week-ahead-26-30-oct-23102026)). In Israel, Prime Minister Netanyahu faces an opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot on Tuesday in a race Reuters described as a coin toss in the polls ([Reuters Take Five via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/take-five-ai-trade-meets-the-fed-4968194)). Israel locked down the West Bank after an attack in Hebron killed two soldiers ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/24/iran-says-wont-allow-us-warships-to-get-close-as-trump-ponders-new-attacks)).
cards.why_it_matters: Brazilian stocks hit a record high after Flávio Bolsonaro's first-round performance, and markets are hoping he wins, according to Reuters. Saxo said investor attention on Israel's vote should focus on what it signals about escalation risks.
cards.what_to_watch: Brazil's result from Monday morning Sydney time.
